title: Pharmacology is up
text: Notes and full transes for the midterm topics, with drugs grouped by mechanism and summary tables. Questions come once we know the exam format.

title: NSTP 1 is up
text: The Bill of Rights: 197 questions, notes and the slides.

title: General Botany is up
text: 522 midterm questions in the teacher's style (scenarios and research methods), notes, charts and transes.

title: Timetable: Pharma moved, NSTP midterm
text: Pharmacology moved to Thursday 1 PM (same topic). NSTP on Friday is the Midterm Exam.

title: Harder mock exams with a predicted grade
text: Mock exam results show Passed or Not passed and your transmuted grade (DMSF handbook). A Difficulty switch picks harder exam-style questions or the practice ones.

title: Psych evals: exam-style questions and matching
text: All 191 Chapter 11–12 questions have a longer exam-style version, plus a matching type part. Preset: 30 MCQ + 30 matching on an answer sheet.

title: Practice again
text: After finishing a section or chapter, redo as many questions as you like. Your mastery never changes.

title: NSTP midterm: Leadership and Health
text: 255 new questions on Leadership Training and Health Awareness, with notes and look-alike drills. The whole midterm coverage is in.

title: NSTP midterm transes and slides
text: One transes PDF for the Bill of Rights, Leadership Training and Health Awareness, plus the slides of both new topics.

title: Notifications
text: This page. Catch up on what's new, get a pop-up when a classmate comments in your course, and choose what you hear about in Settings.

title: Notifications on your phone
text: Get updates even when the site is closed: bell, Settings, then Turn on notifications.

title: NSTP now has comments
text: Ask and answer under any NSTP question, or in the NSTP discussion, before Friday's midterm.

title: Timetable: topics until the finals
text: Weeks 14–19 now show the planned topics from the class matrix, up to the prefinal and comprehensive exams. They're placeholders and may shift.

title: Botany finals: Flower, Fruits and Seeds
text: Lesson 5 is up: 210 questions in her style (scenarios and experiment design), notes, summary tables and a finals transes. Botany now opens on the Finals.

title: Pharmacology finals: Antihypertensives
text: Lesson 6 is up: notes, a summary table of every antihypertensive class, and a finals transes (diuretics, sympatholytics, vasodilators, ACE inhibitors and ARBs, the treatment algorithm).

title: Pharmacology questions are up
text: 564 questions in Dr. Orig's style (drug names from different classes, patient cases), 29 class-matching drills, and an Eval preset (13 MCQ + 2 VSA). Prefinals has 159 hypertension questions, including lots of "what is the BP state?" items for next week's eval.

title: Pharmacology evals (Tue, Oct 27)
text: Pharmacology now opens on "Evals (antihypertensives)". Mock exam → Eval · 13 MCQ + 2 VSA gives mostly drug questions, at most 2 BP-category items, and leaves out the two slides Dr. Orig skipped.

title: Timetable: Pharmacology evals Tuesday
text: Tuesday, Oct 27, 8:00 AM: Pharmacology evals on anti-hypertensive drugs, then the next lesson.

title: Pharmacology: matched to the lecture
text: 47 new questions from what Dr. Orig stressed in class (Lasix, the most potent loop, Jasmine's captopril cough, losartan + amlodipine), a "What Dr. Orig stressed" note, and the parts he didn't teach moved out of the evals.

title: Comments for Botany and Pharmacology
text: Ask and answer under any Botany or Pharmacology question, or in each course's discussion. Pharmacology Lesson 6 also has its picture now.

title: Pharmacology notes: mnemonics for every drug group
text: Each drug group in Notes now ends with a Mnemonic row: famous ones (OH DANG, hyperGLUC, the K+ STAyS, CAPTOPRIL) plus local ones ("Alis ka, renin!", "120/80? Stage 1 na!").

title: Comments now appear instantly
text: New comments show up right away for everyone viewing the same discussion, and course pages get the pop-up and red dot at once instead of up to a minute later.

title: PurCom finals: Nature of Research
text: 68 questions for the research quiz (who said what, which characteristic a case shows, objective → question → hypothesis), notes, and a transes with Dr. Arcena's proposal tips for the prefinal defense and final paper.

title: Math in the Modern World is up
text: Finals Lesson 8, Linear Programming (graphical method): 93 problems with graphs and worked solutions, typed numeric answers, notes and a finals transes. The slides' examples are solved step by step.

title: Math: 20 full LP word problems
text: New chapter of complete word problems (bakery, feed mix, ward staffing, trucks…): read the story, set up the model, graph, test the corners and decide. Each shows the full solution and graph after you answer. Try the new "Quiz · 2 word problems" preset in Mock exam. 253 problems in total.

title: Math quiz practice: 1 given + 2 word problems
text: New section 8-7: 20 problems where the objective and constraints are given, solved completely with graphs. The Mock exam preset now matches the quiz: 1 given-model problem + 2 word problems, 30 minutes. Every practice question now shows its full model, so no more guessing what "Slide example 2" was. 344 problems in total.

title: Exam reminders
text: Get a push notification before exams, evals and quizzes on the timetable. Pick when (up to a week before, or the morning of), what time, and which subjects in Notifications → Settings → Exam reminders. Default: the day before at 7 PM. Needs notifications turned on (iPhone: add the site to your Home Screen first).

title: Quizzes next week: PurCom and Math
text: PurCom quiz on Nature of Research (Wed, Oct 28, 4:00 PM) and Math quiz on Linear Programming (Fri, Oct 30, 7:00 AM) are on the timetable, with exam reminders. The home page now counts down to every test in the next two weeks.

title: Oct 31 is a holiday
text: Saturday, Oct 31 is an institutional holiday: no classes, and the Chem Lab long quiz (Units 15 and 16) is cancelled. New date to follow. It is marked on the timetable.

title: Long weekend: Oct 31 – Nov 3
text: Per DMSFI: Oct 31 institutional non-working day, Nov 1 All Saints' Day, Nov 2 All Souls' Day, Nov 3 Institutional Family Day. No Chem on Saturday (long quiz cancelled) and no Pharmacology on Tuesday, Nov 3. Marked on the timetable.

title: Math now starts at 7:30 AM
text: Math in the Modern World on Fridays is now 7:30–10:00 AM (including next week's LP quiz). Also new on the timetable: tap Week on your phone to see the whole week at once.

title: Smoother site on phones
text: Courses now have a tab bar at the bottom on phones: Home, Practice, Notes, Mock exam and More (topics, discussion, notifications). Pages fade into each other, and the icons are now one matching set.

title: Math: written LP quiz practice (no choices)
text: New sections 8-8 and 8-9: 40 problems answered by writing, like the real quiz: the objective function, the constraints (one per line), the corner points and the final answer. Each part is checked by meaning, so 2x + 2y ≤ 20 counts for x + y ≤ 10. Try Mock exam → Written quiz · 1 given + 2 word problems: every part is scored, like partial credit.

title: New themes: Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Rosé Pine
text: Three popular color themes, each with a light and a dark version. Pick one in any course: Personalize → Colors. It applies to every course and the home page on your device.

title: A fresher look
text: Shorter course headers on phones, answers that react when you check them, confetti when you master a section or pass a mock exam, a calmer dashboard, a loading preview on slow data, two courses per row on the home page, and easier-to-read helper text. Notifications now has a Back button to the page you came from.

title: Fairer answer checking
text: Typed answers no longer accept a different term as a typo (like Section 5 for Section 4, or hypo- for hyper-), and real typos still count. Math written answers now read work like "x = 6, y = 4, P = 460" and labels like "Prep: x + y ≤ 10". Progress is stored more compactly, and if your device's storage ever fills up, you'll see a warning instead of losing answers.

title: Clearer questions in Pharmacology and Psychology
text: In 44 Pharmacology questions the right answer stood out by being the longest; their wrong choices are now just as detailed. Hints no longer give the answer away, and a few Psychology questions got the same fixes. Discussion is now open in every course, and Chem, IML and NSTP now point to the prefinals.

title: Smarter practice
text: Missed questions come back after a few others while the explanation is fresh. Math problems go part by part with your earlier parts in view. Each course shows its next quiz or exam from the timetable, and reviews are timed to land before it. The phone's Back button stays inside the course, courses open instantly, and an "Update ready" banner shows when there's something new.

title: Botany and NSTP question fixes
text: Every Botany and NSTP question now explains its answer, including all of Botany Lesson 5 (flowers, fruits, seeds) and NSTP Health. The right answer is no longer the longest choice: experiment questions now have wrong designs that are just as detailed, each with one flaw to spot.

title: Chem and PurCom question fixes
text: In Chemistry and Purposive Communication, the right answer is no longer the obviously longest choice: 99 questions got wrong choices that are just as specific. Bea's practice exams and the teacher's quizzes stay as written.

title: Daily goal, streak and live quiz
text: Every answer in any course now counts toward a daily goal and streak, shown on the home page with the reviews due in each course. New: Live quiz. Host a quiz for your study group, and everyone joins on their phone with a code. On iPhone Safari, a one-time card shows how to keep your progress safe.

title: Last look before a test
text: The night before a test, open Last look in any course: one page with the questions you missed most and their answers. Hide the answers to test yourself, or print it.

title: Explain it differently, and a daily review reminder
text: Sign in, answer a question, and tap Explain it differently under the feedback for a simpler explanation based on our notes, including exactly why your choice was wrong (30 a day; AI can be wrong, so check your transes). New in Notifications, Settings: a daily review reminder with what is due in each course.

title: Why not your choice, plus two new study tools
text: Pharmacology lesson 6: after a wrong answer, a line now says why the choice you picked is wrong (also in the mock exam review). New: Blurt on the Notes page (write all you remember about a topic, then see what you missed), and, optional in Personalize, How sure are you? (answer Sure or Not sure; confident mistakes come back sooner). Some questions in every course were reworded so the answer can't be guessed from a repeated word.

title: Chem finals: lecture quiz reviewer
text: New in General Chemistry: Topic 12, aromatic compounds (benzene, naming, EAS reactions, directing effects, phenols) and Topic 13, alcohols, amines, ethers and thiols. 387 questions with notes, matching sets and charts, built from the slides, the Oct 24 lecture and the board. Studying for is now set to the Lecture quiz; the Finals exam covers the same topics so far. Aldehydes and ketones will be added once their slides and video lecture are out. The transes PDF was also cleaned up: the empty template pages and placeholder boxes are gone.

title: Chem: written quiz practice
text: Her quizzes are written, so the Chem reviewer now practices that: tricky true or false, type the IUPAC name (every number counts), draw structures and predict products on paper then check yourself, and short essays with key points. Try the Mock quiz (written) preset: 30 items in her quiz order, timed at 60 minutes.

title: Pharma: Eval mock exam for Tuesday
text: The Eval mock exam now feels like his paperless evals: 7 new patient cases (work out the problem, then pick the drug or the next step), 6 lesson questions and 2 VSAs you type at the end, with no true or false. The cases and VSAs only appear in the mock exam (and class challenges made from it). To also practice the cases, turn on Personalize → Include Eval Cases in practice.

title: New address: apmed33.online + pink theme
text: The site now lives at apmed33.online. If you're signed in with Google, your progress comes with you. Your streak, daily goal and notification settings now sync between devices too. New Sakura pink theme in Personalize → Appearance → Colors.

title: Matcha theme, number keys, PurCom slides
text: New Matcha green theme in Personalize → Appearance → Colors. On a keyboard you can now pick answers with 1–5 as well as A–E. Purposive Communication has the Nature of Research slides under Notes & transes.

title: Live quiz sounds + Ocean, Lavender, Coffee
text: The live quiz now has sound: lobby music, a ticking countdown, correct and wrong sounds, a drumroll and a winner fanfare. Tap the speaker in the corner to mute. Three new color themes (Ocean, Lavender, Coffee), and you can now pick colors right on the home page.

title: Slide viewer + mixed look-alike practice
text: Slides (Purposive Communication, NSTP) now open one slide at a time: swipe or use the arrow keys, pinch to zoom, and it remembers where you stopped. Drills → Don't mix up has a new button for a short practice round that switches between look-alike topics.

title: Psychology: why each wrong choice is wrong
text: Psychology chapters 11 and 12 now explain why each wrong choice is wrong: pick a wrong answer in practice and you see a one-line reason, ready for the Evals on Nov 4. Also new: a Warm up button on the home page before a class (when that topic has questions).

title: Chemistry: why each wrong choice is wrong
text: Chemistry topics 12 (Aromatic compounds) and 13 (Alcohols, amines, ethers, thiols) now explain why each wrong choice is wrong. Pick a wrong answer in practice and you get a one-line reason, which helps most for naming and true/false items.

title: Botany: Plant Kingdom (Eval 2) + slides
text: General Botany has a new lesson, Lesson 6: Plant Kingdom, with 149 questions, notes and transes (algae, mosses, ferns, gymnosperms, angiosperms). The Flower, Seed and Fruit slides and the Plant Kingdom slides now open in the slide viewer. The Evals cover both topics (Lesson 5 and Lesson 6); the Eval mock is 30 questions split between them.

title: Pharmacology: Anti-Inflammatory Drugs (Lesson 7)
text: Pharmacology has a new lesson, Lesson 7: Anti-Inflammatory Drugs, for the next evals: 158 questions with why-not lines for every wrong choice, notes with mnemonics, drills, transes, and the slides in the slide viewer. The Mock exam has an Eval 2 preset (13 MCQ + 2 VSA).

title: Botany: why each wrong choice is wrong
text: General Botany Lessons 5 and 6 (Flower, Fruits and Seeds; Plant Kingdom) now explain why each wrong choice is wrong: pick a wrong answer in practice and you see a one-line reason.

title: Pharmacology Evals added to the timetable
text: Evals on Anti-inflammatory drugs are set for Tuesday, Nov 10 (week 16), before GI Drugs 1 and 2.

title: Pharmacology Lesson 7: 12 more cases
text: Twelve new patient cases on anti-inflammatory drugs, and some answer choices reworded so the longest option is not the giveaway.

title: Pharmacology Evals 2 mock updated
text: The Evals 2 mock now uses 7 patient cases and 6 lesson items plus 2 typed questions. The cases are hidden in normal practice (turn them on in Personalize).

title: Tidier color picker
text: The Colors picker is now an even grid of tiles, on the home page and in Personalize.

title: Two Purposive Communication fixes
text: The circular-research choices are reworded so they no longer differ by one word, and the title question now spells out the acronym as your teacher advised.

title: New course icons
text: The home-page pictures are now soft 3D icons in one purple palette, with no background box, so they match your theme in light and dark mode.

title: Daily crossword
text: One short crossword a day, mixing the courses with the nearest evals. Until Wednesday's evals it's Psychology and Botany together, with a tag on each clue. Find it on the home page.

title: Botany evals on Wednesday
text: General Botany has its evals on Wed, Nov 4 (Flower, Fruits and Seeds; Plant Kingdom), the same day as the Psychology evals. The timetable and reminders are updated.

title: Why did I miss it?
text: After a wrong answer, tap why you missed it: didn't know, mixed it up, misread or careless. Your dashboard then shows what trips you up most and lets you practice your mix-ups. Explain it differently now uses the same why-not lines you see.

title: Crossword class board
text: Solve the daily crossword while signed in and your time goes on the class board (first name and last initial; time + 15 seconds per hint). Your puzzle also follows you between your phone and laptop. Don't want to be listed? Tap Hide me under the board.

title: My attendance
text: Signed in? Once the class secretary links your account, a My attendance tile on the home page shows your own attendance from the class tracker, week by week. Only you can see it. Not showing yet? Message the secretary.

title: Link your attendance
text: Signed in but no attendance yet? Tap My attendance on the home page, type your roll number and last name, and the class secretary will link your account.

title: Questions on this slide
text: Reading the Pharmacology Anti-Inflammatory slides? A Quiz button now sits in the slide viewer and opens a free 5-question round on the part you are looking at. It never changes your mastery.

title: Psychology chapters 13 and 14 are up
text: 229 new questions on Psychological Disorders and Methods of Therapy for the Nov 18 evals, checked against the class transes and the book, each with a reason for every wrong choice. A 30 MCQ + 30 matching mock exam is ready too.

title: Pharmacology: why not your choice
text: Lessons 1 to 5 now explain why each wrong choice is wrong, like Lessons 6 and 7. Pick a wrong answer in practice and see the reason.

title: Chemistry: first draft of topics 14 and 15
text: A beginning set of 130 questions on Aldehydes and Ketones and on Carboxylic Acids and Derivatives, made from the slides only. They are in the Finals exam and will be revised after the class discussion.

title: Botany: why not your choice, lessons 1 to 4
text: Every question in Lessons 1 to 4 now explains why each wrong choice is wrong, so all six Botany lessons have it.

title: Questions on this slide: more decks
text: The Quiz button in the slide viewer now also works for the Botany (flower, seed, fruit, plant kingdom), NSTP (Bill of Rights, leadership, health) and PurCom research slides.
